examples: He realized that he had left his umbrella on the train.

wiktionary.gloss: To become aware of, understand, or appreciate (a fact or situation, especially something which has been true for some time).
To sense (something) strongly or vividly as if real.
To cause (something) to seem real; to make realistic; specifically, to present (something) clearly to the mind, a person, (archaic) oneself, etc., so that it seems real.

examples: Near-synonyms: implement, execute; actualize, materialize, embody; accomplish
The objectives of the project were never fully realized.
wiktionary.gloss: To convert (something imaginary or planned, as a goal or idea) into reality; to bring into real existence, to make real.
To achieve (one's) potential.

examples: By realizing the company’s assets, the liquidator was able to return most of the shareholders’ investments.
Profits from the investment can be realized at any time by selling the shares.
wiktionary.gloss: To convert (an asset or property, especially investments such as bonds, shares, etc.) into a more easily usable form such as money, especially by selling the asset or property.

examples: to realize large profits from a speculation
wiktionary.gloss: To acquire (money, a profit, etc.) by selling an asset or property, through trade, etc.; also (followed by on), to make (money or a profit) on an investment, a venture, etc.
Of an asset or property: to generate (a specific amount of money or interest) when invested or sold.

examples: The southern /v/ is realized as the voiced approximant [ʋ].
wiktionary.gloss: To turn (an abstract linguistic object, especially a phoneme) into a speech sound actually used in a language.
To obtain an entity from (an abstract group or structure).
To arrange (a musical work written for a single performer) to be performed by an orchestra; to orchestrate.
To complete (a musical work which is incomplete or not fully notated).
Chiefly in Baroque music: to play an accompaniment, harmonies, etc., based on (a figured bass).
To become aware of or understand a fact or situation.
To cause to seem real; to make realistic.

Followed by on or upon: to acquire money or a profit from the sale of an asset or property.
